results.summary_before: This project measures the duty cycle of an incoming PWM signal on ui[0] and reports a 7-bit value on uo[0] to uo[6], with uo[7] acting as a valid flag. A finite state machine counts how long the input is high within a fixed time window and computes the duty cycle, where 127 corresponds to 100 percent. It runs at 50 MHz and is tested by feeding a PWM signal from a generator and observing the outputs with a logic analyzer. No silicon test results are reported.

results.summary_before: This project is a compact 4-channel fractional-N phase-locked loop (PLL) frequency synthesizer intended for next-generation systems-on-chip. It is controlled via a simple CSR interface using input pins for data and address, and outputs four independent clock channels plus an ADC output for control voltage monitoring. The design is implemented in Verilog and targets a 10 MHz reference clock. The documentation is extremely minimal, providing only pin descriptions and no detailed explanation of operation or testing.
